FULL.notes:
[chunk 1/7] The filing provided is the cover pages, table of contents, forward-looking statements, metrics limitations, financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, comprehensive income statement, stockholders' equity, cash flows), and the beginning of the notes to financial statements for Meta Platforms, Inc. Form 10-Q for Q2 2026 (ended June 30, 2026). No SIFI-material counterparties, investments, commitments, off-balance-sheet entities, or risk signals are explicitly named or disclosed in this excerpt. The document shows boilerplate filing headers, standard financial reporting, and generic disclaimers about estimates and methodologies for user metrics. Revenue is broken down by segment (Family of Apps, Reality Labs) and geography (US/Canada, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Rest of World). No named business relationships, customer concentration data, supplier dependencies, strategic partnerships, or investments beyond the company's own operations are disclosed in the sections provided. The sections mentioning 'Commitments and contingencies' on the balance sheet are not detailed in the excerpt. To extract SIFI-material items, the full Item 1 Business narrative, risk factors (Item 1A), and detailed notes on investments, leases, or commitments would be needed."
[chunk 3/7] KEY FINDINGS: (1) **El Paso Data Center JV / RVG (Severity 4)**: Meta is entering a JV for a data center campus in El Paso, Texas, with 20% ownership and contributing ~$2.3B in assets. Critically, Meta is providing **residual value guarantees of ~$13B max exposure**—this is hidden leverage off-balance-sheet that creates downside protection for the majority owner (uncnamed co-owner). If the co-owner defaults or the asset depreciates sharply, Meta absorbs losses. This is material at 11% of annualized revenue. (2) **Capex/ROI Gap (Severity 3)**: Meta's capex runs ~$31B/quarter ($62B annualized) with aggressive AI infrastructure buildout (cloud, servers, data centers). Reality Labs loses $8.65B per 6 months and is not expected to inflect through 2026. Multi-year R&D horizon creates capex commitment without near-term revenue offset. (3) **RSU Deferred Comp (Severity 2)**: $79.79B in unrecognized RSU expense over 3 years; R&D employee comp nearly doubled YoY. (4) **Ad Revenue Concentration (Severity 3)**: >98% revenue from advertising; exposed to EU DSA enforcement (preliminary findings issued Oct 2025), Apple iOS privacy changes, and regulatory restrictions on targeting/measurement. Apple and Google are critical platform partners and regulators. (5) **Transfer Pricing Tax Contingency (Severity 4)**: $15.89B IRS notice for 2017-2019; plus $18.74B in unrecognized tax benefits as of June 30, 2026. Ongoing Tax Court litigation with high stakes. Represents ~14% of annualized revenue in dispute. No direct CAPEX_COUNTERPARTY relationship disclosed for the El Paso JV co-owner (name withheld; exclusivity agreement only). DSA proceedings and geopolitical risks (Middle East, Russia, Iran internet disruptions) noted but not SIFI-material on their own (regulatory risk, not leverage/circularity).
[chunk 7/7] Source text is boilerplate executive compensation (trading plan modification for Aaron Anderson) and exhibits list. No SIFI-material leverage, circularity, concentration, or hidden risk signals detected. Only substantive entity relationship is Meta's debt indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee—a standard banking service, not SIFI-material by itself. No off-balance-sheet entities, investments in AI labs, strategic partnerships with compute suppliers, or material customer/supplier concentration mentioned in this excerpt."
